questions.question: Which is the first intermediate in the conversion of cholesterol to bile acids?

suspectLines.text: Option A: 7-dehydrocholesterol is an intermediate in the conversion of cholesterol to vitamin D.

questions.explanation:
The first intermediate in the synthesis of bile acids is 7α-hydroxycholesterol.

This reaction is catalyzed by the enzyme 7α-hydroxylase, a microsomal CYP450 enzyme, which requires NADPH, oxygen, and vitamin C as co-factors. It is the rate-limiting step in the synthesis of bile acids.

Regulation of bile acid synthesis occurs by feedback inhibition of 7α-hydroxylase via the Farnesoid X receptor. When the level of bile acids in the enterohepatic circulation increases, FXR is activated and transcription of the enzyme is suppressed.

Other options:
Option A: 7-dehydrocholesterol is an intermediate in the conversion of cholesterol to vitamin D.
Option C: Lanosterol is an intermediate in the synthesis of cholesterol.
Option D: Ergosterol is a sterol found in plants.

questions.question: Which of the following is the main apolipoprotein present in LDL?

suspectLines.text: Which of the following is the main apolipoprotein present in LDL?

questions.question: Which of the following statements about LDL is false?

options.text: It is the marker of cardiovascular disease.

suspectLines.text: Apo B-48 is not the ligand of LDL.

questions.explanation:
Apo B-48 is not the ligand of LDL.

Apo B-48 is the apolipoprotein present on nascent chylomicrons. The main apolipoprotein of LDL (β-lipoprotein) is apo B (B-100), which is found also in VLDL.

Low-density lipoproteins (LDL) deliver cholesterol to the tissues, hence it is a marker of cardiovascular disease.

questions.question: A 56-year-old man suffering from uncontrolled diabetes mellitus came for a routine checkup. His lipid profile revealed increased TG (triacylglycerol) and VLDL (very low-density lipoprotein). What is the cause of this abnormal lipid profile?

options.text: Increased activity of lipoprotein lipase and decreased activity of hormone sensitive lipase
Increased activity of hormone sensitive lipase and decreased lipoprotein lipase activity
Increase in peripheral function of LDL receptors
Increased in activity of hepatic lipase

suspectLines.text: Insulin induces the activity of lipoprotein lipase (LPL) which is present on the capillary walls. LPL promotes hydrolysis of TG and the degradation of the transport proteins, VLDL, and chylomicrons. In diabetes, low insulin leads to decreased LPL activity which corresponds to an increase in VLDL and TG.

questions.explanation:
In chronic diabetes, the values of TG and VLDL are increased due to an increase in hormone-sensitive lipase and a decrease in lipoprotein lipase.

Insulin has an inhibitory effect on hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL). In diabetes, low insulin corresponds to an increase in HSL activity. This promotes the breakdown of lipids and the release of TG and free fatty acids from the adipose tissue.

Insulin induces the activity of lipoprotein lipase (LPL) which is present on the capillary walls. LPL promotes hydrolysis of TG and the degradation of the transport proteins, VLDL, and chylomicrons. In diabetes, low insulin leads to decreased LPL activity which corresponds to an increase in VLDL and TG.
